item.title: Kasugayama Primeval Forest: Nara's Sacred Ancient Woodland — Guide
item.description: Rising behind Kasuga Taisha, the Kasugayama Primeval Forest is one of the most remarkable green spaces in Japan: a genuine virgin forest protected since 841, when hunting and logging were banned to honour the shrine’s gods, and left untouched for nearly 1,200 years. The result is a rare surviving lowland primeval woodland of towering evergreens, ancient cedars and dense undergrowth, alive with birds and deer, forming part of Nara’s World Heritage listing.
